{"self_assessment": "Impact
I proposed the fish, which suited the activity well: its outline is made of gentle curves that dominoes handle easily. I sketched it on the pad and laid the start domino and the first stroke, so the whole picture grew from my sketch. Before the push, about 121 of the 124 standing dominoes were connected to the start, and the fish was recognizable as a fish.

Execution
I laid the top line and carried it from the crossing out to the upper tail tip. I inspected the tail and crossing several times and judged that the chain carried through nearly everything. I left the three stray dominoes by the upper tail alone because they sat against the live line, and I asked everyone to keep their hands off the table before the push so nobody would bump it.

Collaboration
I divided the work at the start: I took the top line, Omar the bottom line, and Hana and Jack the tail. I kept coordinating as the build went on, including telling Hana I would carry the line on from the crossing so we would not wait on each other. I answered Jack's question about the doubled-up joint and kept the table informed with short status updates.

Leadership
I set the direction in the first minute with a clear plan and roles, so the table started building at once rather than debating. I kept the group focused on checking and protecting the result, not tinkering with it. The table finished early with a connected, clean picture.", "my_share_percent": 40}
